Army Gals is a choice-driven visual novel developed and published by Dharker Studios, released on Steam in 2017. The game blends elements of romance, survival drama, and branching storytelling into a narrative-focused experience centered around character interactions and player decisions. While it follows the structure typical of many visual novels—reading dialogue and making choices that influence the outcome—it attempts to distinguish itself by placing the characters in a wilderness survival scenario rather than the usual school or slice-of-life settings commonly seen in the genre. The result is a story that alternates between relationship-building moments and tense situations where the group must deal with isolation and uncertainty.

The story follows Kyle, a young man who has been labeled a troublemaker and sent to a disciplinary outdoor retreat designed to teach responsibility through survival training. Initially expecting a harsh and unpleasant experience, Kyle arrives at the remote camp only to discover that he will be sharing the retreat with three very different girls. At first the situation seems awkward but manageable, as the group prepares to endure the wilderness program under the supervision of the retreat staff. However, the situation quickly becomes far more serious when the group awakens one morning to find that all of the instructors have mysteriously disappeared. With no adults around to guide them and no easy way to leave the remote area, the four teenagers are suddenly forced to survive on their own in the wilderness.

From that point onward, the narrative becomes a mixture of survival storytelling and character development. The group must work together to gather supplies, find shelter, and navigate the unfamiliar environment while trying to figure out what happened to the missing staff members. As the days pass, tensions rise and personal conflicts begin to surface among the group. Each character carries their own background, insecurities, and motivations, which gradually unfold through conversations and shared experiences. The player’s decisions influence how Kyle interacts with the others, shaping the relationships that develop throughout the story.

The gameplay itself is built almost entirely around reading dialogue and making choices at key moments. Players guide Kyle through various conversations and situations by selecting responses that determine how the characters react. Some choices lead to stronger bonds with certain characters, while others may create conflict or alter the direction of events. Because the story branches into multiple narrative paths, different decisions can lead to entirely different scenes, character outcomes, and endings. In some scenarios the focus leans heavily toward romance and emotional bonding, while in others the story becomes darker as the characters struggle with fear, mistrust, or dangerous situations in the wilderness.

The three female characters serve as the central focus of the narrative, each offering a distinct personality and storyline. Their interactions with Kyle and with each other drive much of the emotional tension within the story. Some routes emphasize romantic development and personal growth, while others reveal hidden aspects of the characters’ pasts that influence how they respond to the survival situation. Because the player can pursue different relationships depending on their decisions, replaying the game allows for the discovery of new dialogue, alternate scenes, and different conclusions to the story.

Visually, Army Gals follows the familiar anime-inspired art style commonly used in many visual novels. The character portraits are colorful and expressive, with a variety of facial expressions that change during conversations to reflect emotions such as surprise, anger, or affection. The game also includes a number of illustrated CG scenes that appear during important story moments, highlighting dramatic events or key romantic interactions. The backgrounds depict various wilderness environments such as forests, campsites, and outdoor shelters, helping reinforce the survival theme that underpins the narrative.

The soundtrack contributes to the atmosphere by shifting tone depending on the situation. Calmer music accompanies everyday conversations and lighter character moments, while more intense or suspenseful tracks appear during dangerous or emotional scenes. Although the game does not rely heavily on voice acting, the music and sound effects help guide the player’s emotional response to the unfolding story. The pacing of the audio complements the narrative structure, allowing quieter character interactions to contrast with moments of tension or mystery.

Despite its interesting premise, the game has several weaknesses that become noticeable during play. One of the most commonly mentioned issues is the inconsistency of the writing. Certain character interactions and emotional scenes are engaging and well-paced, while other parts of the narrative feel rushed or underdeveloped. The protagonist himself can sometimes feel passive within the story, reacting to events rather than actively shaping them. This can make it harder for players to feel fully invested in Kyle’s role as the central character.

Another challenge comes from the game’s attempt to balance multiple tones within the same narrative. The story shifts between romance, survival drama, and moments of mystery, which can occasionally feel uneven. Some players may appreciate the unpredictable mixture of genres, while others may feel that the transitions between lighthearted romantic scenes and darker survival elements are not always handled smoothly. The blend of these different storytelling styles sometimes gives the impression that the game is unsure whether it wants to focus more on romance or suspense.

Even with these shortcomings, Army Gals still offers an enjoyable experience for fans of choice-driven storytelling. The branching narrative structure provides multiple endings and encourages players to replay the game to explore different routes and uncover hidden story elements. Those who enjoy visual novels that focus on character relationships and moral choices will likely find the experience engaging, especially when experimenting with different decisions to see how the story changes.

In the end, Army Gals stands as a modest visual novel that attempts to combine romance with a wilderness survival narrative. While its writing and pacing occasionally struggle to maintain consistency, the game still provides a few memorable character moments and several branching story paths that reward exploration. For players interested in interactive narratives that mix relationship drama with a slightly darker premise, it offers a unique take on the visual novel format.

The main problem with this game is that it has some moments where the outcomes of choices are very unpredictable and unfair. This is one of those visual novels where one small choice can instantly lock you into a specific outcome for the long-term game even when the causality of how it could possibly do that doesn't really make sense. It commits the huge game design sin of sometimes just arbitrarily throwing the player under the bus even if the player acts rationally and benevolently at every step. 

Thus, the game will sometimes seem to just force players into bad endings for seemingly no reason from the player's perspective. This can make the ending feel more like a random kick in the face sometimes, rather than like a rationally designed and compelling story, if you are just randomly unlucky enough.

However, if it wasn't for these kinds of unpredictable and irrationally designed choices, then the game would be good overall. 

There are three things in specific where most of the problems seem to come from. Knowing these three things will do a lot to make you less likely to just randomly get a bad ending that you can't control. Here they are, so that you have a better chance of being able to enjoy yourself without being forced to use a complete walkthrough guide:

[spoiler]
(1) When you encounter a crashed car then you MUST choose to either look under the car or at the tires as one of your two allowed choices. The game only allows you to search two spots on the car before you "run out of time" and you can't choose more. You'll also want to find some food supplies in the car too. Not searching under the car or the tires will instantly doom you to not being able to get any of the good endings.

(2) When presented with choices of which girl to talk to each night, never talk to the same girl two nights in a row. If you do so, then you will be silently punished for it in the character relationship system. Players have no way of predicting this in the game. It's just yet another way the developers will randomly throw you under the bus if you pick the "wrong" choices for something that is essentially fundamentally unpredictable and unfair. These nightly conversation choices are one of the worst parts of the game due to the fact that it is so easy for them to go bad and for the girls to all start always responding coldly to you for the rest of the entire game.

(3) The characters magically know what you've said or done with other characters, even when this is physically impossible and there's no way they possibly could. This is true from the very beginning of the game. Keep that in mind in how you make your choices.
[/spoiler]

The underlying character relationship system of the game overall is not very well designed.

Also, the game fails to tell you some of its hotkeys and also never bothers explaining what any of the extra buttons do. Here are two of the most important ones:

- Pressing the "H" key will hide the dialog box and buttons so that you can view the scene without anything being blocked from view.

- The button labeled "SK" in the bottom right is for skipping through text until you encounter text you haven't encountered before or a choice. This is based on persistent tracking of what you've seen before when playing the game.

Also, you should be aware that there's an adult patch available from the official site for the game, if you want to see that kind of thing. When installing the patch though, they confusingly tell you to put the file into the "game" directory, but what they mean by this is that you have to put it into ".../Army Gals/game" and not merely in ".../Army Gals/". There is a literal folder named "game" inside of the game folder for Army Gals. This may confuse some users and make them think that the adult patch doesn't actually work. Watch out for this pitfall, so you don't get confused. I don't understand why the developers don't realize how confusing this is.

Steam doesn't let me give a neutral rating, so I'm rating this as negative because of the fact that unpredictable choices that have huge consequences in the game outcomes are such an incredibly bad game design mistake. Otherwise though, the game  is generally fairly enjoyable. You just need to be aware of the hidden gotchas that I've covered above and then you'll have a much more pleasant experience.

Army Gals is a survival adventure visual novel both developed and published by Dharker Studio. You take on the role of Kyle, a juvenile deliquent who swears that he DIDN'T do it, of whom is sent by his parents to a behaviorial modification retreat in order to "better" himself. C'mon, that's just a cleaner way of saying this is a camp for bad kids and we all know it! Anyhow, after a short greeting at the train station from the camp counselors, Kyle reluctantly makes his way to the campgrounds where he meets three other problematic youths in the form of a trio of beautiful yet vastly different and troubled young women also sent to the camp for other dubious behavioral reasons. After only one night there, the four youths awaken the next morning and find that the camp counselors, who left for town the previous day to get supplies, have still not returned so it's up to Kyle and the group of women to fend for themselves while stranded deep in the wilderness and left to their own devices. Will they be able to stay alive and find their way back to civilization? How will this nature bound experience pan out...turn the page?  

[h1]PRESENTATION[/h1]

The title boasts some rather impressive illustrations as does most of Dharker Studios offerings. The manga-inspired art is fantastic with lots of beautiful colors and the backgrounds are just as alluring. You have a number of choices to make as the story progresses so that alone really helps to keep the narrative interesting. As far as technicalities, the novel ran smoothly and I didn't see any typos that I can remember? Aurally, this visual novel has a fairly good soundtrack and a number of ambient sound effects included which really helps with immersion while you read the story. Also, there is no voiced dialogue which is great for me as I prefer my visual novels without it. In the end, this V.N. offers up quite an impressive visual and auditory presentation that really compliments the intriguing storyline. 

[h1]CONCLUSION[/h1]

Like most of Dharker Studios visual novels, Army Gals was a completely enjoyable and terrific read with a wonderfully penned story, many tension breaking humorous moments and great music all wrapped up in a very professional and well put together package. I have to admit though that my first playthrough had a rather...dark ending which I won't go into for fear of spoilers but it definitely stayed on my mind for quite some time after completion. With that said, replayability is high as there are many different decisions to make in the branching narrative that could lead to vastly different outcomes depending on your selections. Option-wise, there are a number of Steam Achievements to hunt down and Steam Trading Cards to collect. Also, the novel has the basic V.N. options for music/sound volume and text speed as well as a C.G. gallery that unlocks as the story progresses. D.L.C. is available in the form of an impressive original soundtrack, a gorgeous set of wallpapers, digital dakimakuras and a fun poker game. In summary, Army Gals takes you on an elightening and fun adventure filled with mystery, tough choices, emotional moments, possible romance and intrigue so it is HIGHLY RECOMMENDED to fans of the visual novel genre.

Army Gals можно вполне сравнить с коробкой конфет с очень яркой упаковкой. В первую очередь она цепляет взгляд, или наоборот - отталкивает, своим: «посмотрите на меня! тут есть фансервис и бесплатный патч с 18+ контентом! заплатите и подр****е!» Вот только не всё так просто. Почитав некоторые обзоры, я зацепился за упоминание о довольно интересном сюжете, который многие хвалили. В основном, только те, кто купили игру из-за "яркой упаковки" (или «знатоки» ВН) жаловались на его странную последовательность или банальность. И в первые минуты тебя действительно сразу встречает «яркая упаковка», усиливая подозрения. И только преодолев начальную «распаковку», начинаешь пробовать «конфеты» на вкус, и они не такие приторные, как кажется на первый взгляд. Пусть кто-то говорит, что «всё это уже было», но сюжет действительно цепляет. Это не банальная школьная ВН, которая концентрируется на школьных проблемах и романтике в тепличных условиях – атмосфера этой игры включает в себя небольшие элементы детектива, выживания и даже немного мистики, которые увлекают тебя в центр истории. 

Кратко о минусах и плюсах:

Минусы. Явно больших минусов я не увидел, это скорее лично мои придирки:
-Музыка. Иногда треки меняются на «тревожные», повышая давление в местах, где это не нужно. Но в целом музыка приятная и атмосфере не мешает.
-Выбор ответов. Порой неочевиден, потому периодически «рандомен», что можно отнести и к плюсам, и к минусам.
-Игра в принципе короткая

Требования:
Как всегда, знание английского языка или поиск русификатора (не проверял, есть ли). Для тех, кто с ним дружит – проблем нет.

Плюсы:
+Сюжет. Отличная история со своими небольшими твистами, которая цепляет и постепенно затягивает в игру.
+Большая вариативность выбора. Такого количества разных концовок я уже давно не видел не только в ВН, но и вообще в любой другой игре. Ложкой дёгтя является, как я писал выше, «рандомность» некоторых выборов. Небольшой спойлер для подогрева - тут даже можно умереть ;)
+Атмосфера. Сколько бы не косились на «скудные задники» - их достаточно, и ощущения, что ты проводишь всю историю в одних и тех же локациях не возникает, чему помогает сюжет, музыка и сами персонажи.
+Хорошо прописанные персонажи. Их хоть и не назовешь уникальным, но у каждого есть линия поведения, своя история за плечами и свои интересы, которые приходится выяснять по небольшим порциям.
+Главный герой. Не тряпка, не обладает синдромом «героя-ловеласа», ведет себя вполне адекватно, остальное зависит от вашего выбора действий. 

Отдельно можно сказать пару слов про патч. Он опционален, хотя без него игра будет «обрезана», и чуть потеряет в атмосфере. Установка патча легкая (скачиваешь файл и просто кидаешь в директорию, даже без установки) и не лочит ачивки (даже добавляет одну уникальную)

Итог. Игра стоит своих денег (но дождаться скидки никто не запрещает) и стоит времени, потраченного на неё.
